title: Making Things Without Code
hook: Describe an app, a website, or a little tool in plain English, and AI will write the code and build a first version. 'Vibe coding' lets non-programmers make software — within limits.
key_points: AI can turn a plain-language description into a working first draft of software.
Newer 'build an app' tools handle the code so you don't have to learn it.
Great for prototypes, personal tools, and learning — shaky for anything serious.
It can write insecure or broken code; don't ship sensitive projects unchecked.
content_html: One of the more astonishing recent shifts is that you no longer strictly need to know how to program to make software. Describe what you want in plain English — "a simple website for my dog-walking business," "a tool that splits a bill among friends," "a quiz to help my students study" — and AI will write the underlying code and assemble a working first version. The nickname for this loose, conversational style is "vibe coding": you steer by describing and reacting, and the AI handles the technical details. A wave of "build an app by chatting" tools has made this accessible to people who've never written a line of code.
extra_html: This genuinely opens doors. Hobbyists build little personal tools, small-business owners spin up a basic site or automation, teachers make custom classroom aids, and curious people finally turn a long-held idea into something they can click on. It's also a wonderful, low-pressure way to learn how software works, since you can ask the AI to explain what it just wrote. But it's important to know the ceiling. AI-generated code can be subtly broken, inefficient, or — more worryingly — insecure, all while looking perfectly convincing, and it can struggle as a project grows in complexity. That's fine for a prototype, a personal gadget, or a throwaway experiment. It's risky for anything handling other people's data, money, or privacy, where real software-engineering judgment (and a security review) still matters. Think of it as a remarkably capable apprentice that lets you build things you couldn't before — as long as you don't mistake a quick draft for a finished, trustworthy product.

related.title: AI Agents: AI That Does Things
related.hook: A chatbot answers; an agent acts. The new frontier is AI that can browse, click, book, and complete multi-step tasks for you — powerful, and exactly why you keep it on a leash.

related.title: AI at Work
related.hook: The biggest everyday payoff from AI is at work: drafting the email, summarizing the meeting, untangling the spreadsheet formula. The trick is using it without leaking secrets or trust.

related.title: What AI Can't Do
related.hook: Today's AI can write a sonnet and flunk a question a child gets right. Knowing its hard edges — no real understanding, no live truth, no common sense — is what makes you good at using it.

flashcards.prompt: What can AI 'build an app' tools do for a non-programmer?

choices.text: Turn a plain-English description into a working first version of software
Nothing — you must learn to code first

flashcards.explanation_html: These tools generate the code from your description, letting non-coders make prototypes and personal tools — though the results need checking and aren't bulletproof.

flashcards.prompt: What's the main caution with AI-generated code?
flashcards.back_html: It can be broken or insecure while looking fine. Great for prototypes and learning; risky to ship for anything sensitive without expert review.
